records.Concise description: An early Bitcoin-native animated/generative art series built as looping on-chain works, with its first chapter inscribed extremely early in Ordinals history.
records.Deeper researched summary: Ordinal Loops is associated with some of the earliest ambitious animated artwork on Ordinals. Historical material places its first chapter among sub-1k inscriptions and emphasizes Bitcoin-native looping/generative aesthetics. Current public project activity has persisted into the 2025–2026 window, so the registry treats it as active, while avoiding unqualified 'first fine art' marketing claims.
Creators / founders: Project creator attribution requires archival first-party confirmation before final public lock
records.Launch / history: First chapter created during the earliest 2023 Ordinals period, with works commonly cited in approximately the #452–#641 range; later chapters continued the series.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: It demonstrated that early inscriptions could be designed as time-based/animated art rather than static collectibles and occupies rare sub-1k provenance.
records.Verification basis: Historical independent coverage, current social presence from research pass, and Ordinals indexing.
Research notes / uncertainties: Project 'first fine art collection' language is a project/marketing claim and should not be presented as settled fact.
Creator identity and canonical project URL should be first-party archived before publication.

records.Concise description: A 21-piece early Ordinals collection inscribed consecutively around #356–#377 and focused on Bitcoin/timechain imagery.
records.Deeper researched summary: Timechain Collectibles is a small, extremely early collection valued chiefly for consecutive sub-1k provenance. Historical reporting places the works around inscriptions #356–#377 in late January 2023. The project does not show enough verified ongoing development to classify it active, so it is preserved as a historical artifact.
Creators / founders: Creator attribution not sufficiently verified in the current research pass
records.Launch / history: Approximately January 30, 2023; 21 works inscribed consecutively in the mid-300s inscription range.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: Its consecutive sub-1k placement makes it an important reference in the chronology of coordinated early Ordinals collections.
records.Verification basis: Historical independent coverage and Ordinals indexer chronology.
Research notes / uncertainties: Creator attribution and exact canonical website require archival verification before public publication.

records.Concise description: A 512-piece early Ordinals collection inscribed around #58,735–#60,326.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitcoin Bandits is a finite early collection whose main importance is chronological: it predates the mature large-collection market and is indexed in the roughly 58k–60k inscription range. Current indexers retain the collection, but evidence for an ongoing project roadmap/community is insufficient, so it is classified historical.
Creators / founders: Creator attribution unresolved in the current research pass
records.Launch / history: Inscribed during early 2023; 512 works commonly indexed across approximately #58,735–#60,326.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: It helps document the transition between sub-10k experiments and the later wave of large 10k collections.
records.Verification basis: On-chain-history catalog and current indexer presence.
Research notes / uncertainties: Creator/founder remains unresolved; keep profile historical and fact-light until first-party archive is found.

records.Concise description: A 10,000-piece Ordinals collection built around tombstone, obituary, and Bitcoin-history motifs.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitcoin Burials uses the visual language of memorials and graves to encode Bitcoin/crypto cultural references into a large PFP-like collection. The project remains indexed and its standalone site is still identifiable, but the mint is finite and current first-party development activity is not strong enough to classify it active.
Creators / founders: Creator/founding team not sufficiently verified in the current research pass
records.Launch / history: Launched during the 2023 Ordinals collection wave as a 10,000-piece project.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: It is a recognizable example of Ordinals using memorial/obituary imagery to comment on Bitcoin history and crypto culture at 10k scale.
records.Verification basis: Project site identity plus current indexer visibility; active development not established.
Research notes / uncertainties: Founder attribution and recent activity require stronger first-party evidence if Command Center wants an ACTIVE classification.
